title: The Orchard of Rosewater Lane
premise: Ansel Reyes, a ghostwriter who vanished from public life twelve years ago after a scandal that cost him his name, is hired to write the memoirs of celebrated vintner Marguerite Voss—only to discover she has inherited half of an orchard on Rosewater Lane, co-owned with the one person who knew him before: Juniper Hale, the woman whose testimony once saved him and whose silence he never explained. Forced onto the same stubborn acreage neither can sell without the other, they spend a season untangling the deed, the old betrayal, and the memoir Ansel is secretly writing about her closest friend. When Marguerite discovers the ghostwriter's identity and threatens to expose him, Ansel must choose between the anonymity that kept him safe and claiming his name—and Juniper—publicly, before the last ferry of the season carries away his chance. He signs the orchard over to shared ownership under his real name, testifies to the truth he buried, and boards the ferry not to flee but to bring Juniper back with him.
about_author: Cyrus Marchetti is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories set in coastal towns where everyone knows your business. His work explores how people rebuild themselves out of small mercies and stubborn land.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hired by Marguerite Voss to ghostwrite her memoirs, Ansel travels to Rosewater Lane to research an inherited orchard and finds Juniper Hale's name beside his own history in the county records. The emotional beat: dread sharpening into recognition—the past has found a legal address.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She returns to tend the dying apple trees her grandmother left her, expecting solitude, and instead meets the man she testified for a decade ago wearing someone else's name. The beat: fury braided with relief that he's alive, and the resolve not to show either.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Neither will sell; the lawyer says joint tenancy means joint decisions. They negotiate a fragile truce—one week each on the property—while Ansel begins interviewing Marguerite, whose stories keep circling dangerously close to his old scandal. The beat: wary cooperation with electricity underneath.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Clearing storm damage, they uncover letters proving the original deed was fraudulently transferred—a theft that ruined both their families differently. The beat: grief becoming purpose; the orchard stops being an obstacle and becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Marguerite asks him to include 'the Reyes affair' in her memoir as a cautionary tale, forcing him to shape his own ruin into someone else's narrative. The beat: self-erasure as survival, and the first crack in it—he writes one true sentence and cannot delete it.

chapters.title: Harvest Without Permission
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Defying the injunction stalling the estate, they harvest together through one long golden day, neighbors drifting in to help. The beat: joy as an act of defiance; almost-confession at dusk, interrupted by a call from Marguerite's publisher asking pointed questions.

chapters.title: The Name in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Marguerite reads his draft, recognizes his voice from an old article, and confronts him: help her win the orchard outright and she stays silent; refuse and she exposes him. The beat: blackmail dressed as generosity, and the sick clarity that safety was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: Ferry Schedules and Other Lies
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Discovering Ansel's deal with Marguerite, Juniper assumes the worst—that he came back only to take what little she has left. She packs. The beat: heartbreak repeating its oldest pattern; the last ferry of the season posted on the dock board like a countdown.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the probate hearing on the fraudulent transfer, instead of hiding, Ansel takes the stand under his real name, telling the whole truth—his crime, his exile, Juniper's sacrifice. Marguerite's leverage dies in open court. The beat: climax; identity reclaimed at the highest price, publicly and irreversibly.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Ansel signs the orchard into shared trust, then runs for the final crossing—not fleeing but fetching Juniper, who chose the mainland out of pride. On the deck he offers her not escape but partnership: the trees, the truth, the name. The beat: resolution; two people done being invisible, planting something that outlasts them.
